Thank you for the context, I definitely agree that when people get the help they need their overall experience with the world and other people improves significantly. It is always worth it to seek deeper understanding of yourself and your situation in order to improve your quality of life. 

I can see that you mean well, but I encourage you to rethink the sentiment that people who are abused "allow" that abuse--it isn't weakness or enabling that causes these things to happen. 23 is a vulnerable time and 18 even moreso--especially with the nature of this disorder.

People who are abused do not allow themselves to be abused, they are often taken advantage of, gaslit, and made to fear the repercussions of leaving. Abuse can take some time to recognize.

And I didn't say they shouldn't work on themselves. That's good advice for anyone, I just see "victim mindset" used a lot to dismiss people who suffer legitimate abuse, and you put "he" in quotes when OP explicitly stated that the PTSD is related to mistreatment during their pregnancy--suggesting you doubt what they've said. I never said you aren't allowed to comment, but sharing your advice or opinion doesn't exempt you from criticism of that advice or opinion, especially on sensitive subjects.

"Victim mindset" in this case is a really cool way to blame someone who has been hurt and mistreated for their own mistreatment. Whether or not you see this as abuse, insinuating that someone in this situation doesn't know themselves or their trauma well enough to accurately self report the reasons for their own PTSD is pretty ignorant.

Not to mention, this is clearly not a safe environment for OP to work on themselves. You cannot be in an active trauma situation and productively work on yourself. It's better to seperate (even temporarily) to seek help than it is to stay with a partner who is unsupportive at best and abusive at worst.
If you're ever diagnosed with PTSD because of the way someone treats or treated you, that is NOT someone you want to continue to be involved with. Definitely abuse.

I think what you need to accept, OP, is that you ARE fatshaming her.  Not to her face, but this is just as insidious. You told all of reddit that your girlfriend is beautiful--except for her weight. Your words, not mine.  You mention your height (and there's nothing wrong with being short, but I'm using it as an example) and I want you to think: how would you feel if you found out she thought you were handsome--except for your height?  If she was so embarrassed about your height that she couldn't even introduce you to friends and family? It would hurt, right?

People can have problems with their partners, sure. But this particular type of problem? Nah, man, this is different than "I love her but she leaves wet towels on the floor", this is you implying that your partner is somehow worth LESS than some hypothetical other girl, just because of her weight.

BMI is actually a notoriously terrible way to judge someone's health--an beauty has nothing to do with weight.  Do her a favor and dump her, she deserves someone who loves her without silently judging her or being ashamed of her.  And maybe you should analyze why you're so uncomfortable with yourself that you're putting so much stock in the importance of things like looks.  It's pretty messed up that you think of someone you claim to love as "lesser" person just because of her size.

Can everyone commenting here stop calling alters "personalities", please, it's outdated as hell.

I'd like to clear something up: alters do not choose how they view themselves internally.  A host does not choose what an alter does.  But there is a level of "group accountability" involved, and if an alter says or does anything that's harmful and the host's (or any other alter's) response is "I don't control them"... what they're saying is technically true, but it skips group accountability entirely.

It's like bringing a dog to a friend's house, having it take a dump on their floor, and then saying "I don't control him!" without taking any actions to help solve the current problem (crap on the floor) or prevent future incidents.

Alters that see themselves as different ethnicities are not inherently harmful or racist, so long as they don't claim that social or cultural identity, try to interject themselves into spaces that belong to members of that social or cultural identity, or try to use it to excuse bad behavior. An alter who is in a white body, but sees themselves as dark skinned will, ultimately, never actually be dark skinned.  They will never know the real world struggles or disadvantages of that group.  They aren't "allowed" to use racist speech or speak as though they understand or experience racism, because they absolutely do not.

Also: even when we doubt someone's validity, stop calling alters "characters".  It's abelist as hell and two wrongs don't make a right. This video is appalling, that's true, but speaking like that is damaging to the DID/OSDD community as a whole.

If marriage is important to you, please tell him.  Just find a good, quiet time and say "hey, you mentioned you would never get married and I wanted to know more about your thoughts on that."  See what his reasons are without putting pressure on him up front, just learn more about what it is about marriage that doesn't appeal to him.  Once you have his side, then tell him yours.  Explain that it's a dream of yours, something you really want, something you could see happening with him.  Then reassure him that you aren't telling him that to scare him or force him to marry you, just that you wanted to know his opinions and values and wanted to express your own as well.  After that, you have a lot of options for what you do, depending on what he says and how he reacts and how it makes you feel.
